scope: Board judgements before new sample searches/classifier output. These reuse known public positions, not a holdout. A legal recapture defeats simple retained-pawn arithmetic but does not disprove a sacrifice or mate.

cases.judgement: Rxh5+ forces an interposition with the h-file invasion and open g-file. Inspect the mating continuation; a mere pawn badge may miss the lesson.
Rxg2+ invades the king shelter with queen/bishop support. The rook is not directly capturable, but king-attack mechanisms or mate may outrank the pawn.
Rxc3+ permits Rxc3. This is not an independently retained pawn; the quieter exchange-up structure must not make it a good sacrifice by assumption.
Qxh2+ permits Kxh2; any rook/bishop mating compensation needs separate proof, not a pawn-gain claim.
Rxe5+ permits Qxe5. The second rook is active but no immediate recovery of the offered rook is established.
Early Qxd7+ hangs the queen to several legal recapturers. Reject an ordinary checking-pawn win.
Qxg7+ permits Qxg7 with a supporting rook nearby. Check whether the queen exchange is a mating mechanism; do not count the pawn in isolation.
Qxd7+ is a capturable queen offer in the opening. The advanced f-pawn does not by itself establish compensation.
Qxd7+ has multiple simple queen recaptures. A check is not compensation for this queen donation.
Nxh3+ permits either gxh3 or Qxh3. Any king-attack compensation is unresolved; no retained pawn assumed.
Bxh7+ is a potential thematic bishop sacrifice but both king and knight can capture. A Greek-gift claim needs the full defence analysis.
Qxh3+ permits Qxh3; the passed d-pawn and remaining bishop require independent assessment. Not an elementary pawn win.
Qxf6+ is the previously reviewed mating deflection. Preserve the forced mate and actual deflection ahead of a checking-pawn badge.
Rxg7+ permits Qxg7. Queen support and king exposure may justify it, but the rook offer needs separate proof.
Qxh4+ permits Kxh4. Black's already overwhelming material advantage cannot certify this queen donation as a pawn-winning tactic.
Qxf2+ permits Kxf2. Development/extra material elsewhere is not immediate compensation for the queen.
Another early Qxd7+ queen donation with several recaptures. Keep the positional opening distinct from this unsound candidate.
Qxg3+ permits pawn, king or queen recapture. It is not the Rxf2+ tempo tactic in the same position.
Rxg2 is immediate checkmate. Checkmate must lead, not a newly won pawn.
Bxf7+ in the Evans-style opening permits Kxf7. Do not label an unsupported bishop sacrifice a pawn win.
Qxg6+ permits both knight and h-pawn captures. Require a separate mating/combination proof if anything is displayed.
Qxf7+ permits Rxf7 while White's other rook can be involved. The exchange and any tactical compensation need checking; no simple retained pawn.
Qxg2+ attacks king and Rh1, but Nf2 can interpose while defending that rook. Do not assume a forced rook-winning fork; a smaller checking capture may be the actual local gain.
Bxf7+ is a Legal-style mating combination after the queen has been taken on d1. The mate, not the captured pawn, should lead.
Qxe6+ permits four different recaptures. Any attractive mate pattern must survive all of them; do not credit a simple pawn gain.
Rxb3+ permits axb3. The active knight and king do not establish enough immediate compensation for that rook.
Rxf2+ is the diagnosed tempo capture. All king evasions require distinct safe continuations; a single Qe7 line is insufficient.
Bxe6+ donates the bishop to king or bishop in a blocked bishop ending. No pawn-break compensation is established.
Qxa2+ permits Kxa2 or Nxa2. The locked middlegame and opposite-side castling are not evidence that this queen sacrifice works.
Qxg6+ permits bishop, queen and f-pawn recaptures. Any move-order or attacking compensation must be independently proved.
